rows.t: F-BUDGET No nightly budget or quality floor was supplied
rows.d: The brief makes cost and quality the higher priority, but no ceiling was given, so the site cannot rank hotels by value. It ranks only on confirmed fit (same property as the venue)

rows.t: F-QUALITY No official quality metric is collected
rows.d: Star ratings and review scores come from third parties, which this project's rules exclude as evidence. With no official quality figure, 'quality is a higher priority than distance

rows.t: F-FEE-WYNN Resort fee for Wynn / Bellagio / ARIA / Caesars properties not verified this session
rows.d: Only the Venetian/Palazzo fee ($55 + tax) was re-read today. Treasure Island's $49.95 and the 13.38% tax are carried from an earlier session. Other properties are blank rather than

rows.t: F-PARKING Parking cost not re-read this session
rows.d: Carried from an earlier reading of the hotel terms page, which would not load for this session. Parking is only relevant if driving, and it is excluded from the nightly figures.

rows.t: F-CI Monitor workflow needs a first real run on the default branch
rows.d: The daily re-check is wired as a scheduled GitHub Actions job that commits data back to the branch it ran on. Its first scheduled run after merge is what turns 'last checked' into

rows.t: For each candidate one-day event, does the room allow re-entry, rebuys or an add-on - and can it say so in writing?
rows.d: A yes/no per event number, in writing, for the events you would actually play.

rows.t: Which exact dates, how many nights, and how many guests?
rows.d: Arrival/departure dates, guest count, room count. Without them there is no checkout total, no cancellation deadline and no like-for-like comparison.

rows.t: What is the per-night budget ceiling and the minimum acceptable quality standard?
rows.d: A number and a standard (for example 'not above $X all-in per night').

rows.t: Which walking routes are actually within 30 minutes of the Venetian poker room, door to door?
rows.d: Minutes for every candidate hotel, with the source and date of that measurement.

rows.t: When does each event really end - or how late can you leave one and still make the next?
rows.d: Expected finish, or a scheduled Day 1 end, for the events you want to stack.

rows.t: Is there a real 8 AM start anywhere on the Strip in this window?
rows.d: Any 8 AM start at any room, or acceptance that the day begins at 10:10 AM.

rows.t: For events with no published guarantee, is there one at all?
rows.d: Guarantee yes/no and amount.

rows.t: What is the true all-in cost of a night at each candidate hotel for my dates - rate, fee, tax, parking, refundable or not?
rows.d: One dated itemised quote per hotel, identical dates and occupancy, plus the cancellation deadline.

rows.t: Does the conditional poker rate apply to this trip at all?
rows.d: Whether a $200 buy-in satisfies the qualifying play, and which rate attaches to which building on which date.

rows.t: Which data set is authoritative when the repo's folders disagree?
rows.d: A decision on one canonical source, with the rest archived as read-only.

rows.t: Should the trip be timed to a different series instead?
rows.d: A comparable verified schedule for any other series in the window.

rows.t: What counts as confirmed here, and who may change a label?
rows.d: An agreed policy line on the shared board (evidence required, and who may flip unverified to confirmed).

rows.t: Promote one canonical data set and archive the rest
rows.d: Six folders publish the same series with different labels; a reader can act on a row another folder marks unverified. One source removes the contradiction.

rows.t: Store the room's written answer, then let labels flip automatically
rows.d: Q1 is the real blocker. A per-event rules_confirmed object holding the quote, date and channel lets the badge change itself and shows what justified it.

rows.t: Extend the rate log to full checkout totals
rows.d: Rate + fee + tax is still not what you pay. The log already reserves fields for checkout_total, nightly_average, mandatory_fee, tax, parking, cancellation_deadline and rate_timesta

rows.t: Parse other rooms' daily schedules into the same schema
rows.d: Once a Wynn or Bellagio page parses, the same rule audit and overlap check apply, and the plan stops being single-property.

rows.t: Make the walk check a stored, dated observation
rows.d: Minutes change with construction and entry point. A dated observation with the route link is auditable; a remembered number is not.

rows.t: Write the verification policy on the board and enforce it in CI
rows.d: Most irregularities in this repo came from sessions calling a row verified on inference. One policy line plus a verifier gate makes it structural.

rows.t: Add a change-triage view listing only rows whose source moved
rows.d: A daily re-check is noise unless changed rows surface in one place with before/after quotes; the state file already stores hashes and change dates.

rows.t: Rank on money actually entering the pool, not the advertised buy-in
rows.d: The sheets show the fee is withheld FROM the buy-in ($58 of $300 to the house, $242 to the pool) and some flights discount the fee for early registration, so pool-per-entry is the

rows.t: Keep a 'do not book yet' banner until Q1 and Q2 close
rows.d: The biggest risk is paying for a trip on a plan that assumed freezeout play. The banner is the cheapest control.

rows.t: Record actual field sizes after each event
rows.d: Guarantee/entry is descriptive; entries actually recorded is the number that matters. Post-event counts turn the ratio into evidence across a series.

rows.t: Fail loudly when an official page stops being readable
rows.d: The Wynn page returned the home page twice. Storing final URL, title and byte count turns 'no data' into a visible problem instead of a silently stale row.

rows.t: Keep bounty, satellite, seniors, ladies and other-game events out of the ranking
rows.d: The brief asks for them in a separate section; it also stops a $8,000 pool that includes bounties from being compared with a plain $10,000 pool.
